methods.label: Find the fraction of time that is not green
methods.explanation:
Interpret the randomly chosen time as uniformly placed within a cycle, so equal-length portions of the cycle are equally likely. The light is not green whenever it is yellow or red. These times do not overlap, and together they last
\[
5+30=35\text{ seconds}.
\]
The probability is therefore the non-green duration divided by the full cycle duration:
\[
\frac{35}{60}=\frac7{12}.
\]
The exact switching instants have no duration and do not change this probability. The answer is \(\frac7{12}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
methods.levelReason: This is an elementary time-fraction probability calculation requiring only addition and fraction reduction.

candidate.annotationRationale: A uniform time within one cycle is a uniform point in a time interval, so the relevant target is favorable duration divided by total duration. Fraction meaning and reduction support the arithmetic. The method does not treat the three colors as equally likely outcomes.
limitations: The calculation interprets a randomly chosen time as a uniformly chosen position within the 60-second cycle. Switching instants have probability zero under this model.
